Large language models have transformed the way we interact with computers. At their core, they operate on sequences of tokens rather than raw characters, which means the same sentence can be represented very differently depending on the tokenizer. Understanding these differences is essential for engineers who want to control costs, respect context windows, and design robust prompts. This dashboard compares the output of three popular tokenizers side by side so that the impact of language, code, and formatting choices on token counts becomes immediately visible.
